original_question: Find a compact set K contained in the real line for which the Green function g_{C\K} has two-sided Hölder behavior near K. That is, determine whether there exists α>0 and constants C1,C2>0 such that, for all z with sufficiently small δ=dist(z,K), one has C1·δ^α ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2·δ^α.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 3: the "two-sided Hölder" Green function problem for a compact set on the real line.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly asks for a compact set on the real line, uses the Green function of the complement, formulates the desired two-sided Hölder estimate in terms of δ = dist(z,K), and keeps the problem at the existential level ('find' / 'does there exist') rather than broadening it to a classification problem.
missing_details: Section 2 has a standing assumption that K is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, so g_{ℂ\K} is continuous throughout ℂ.
The notation g_{ℂ\K} means the Green function of ℂ \ K with pole at infinity; that role of the Green function is stated earlier in the notation/background.
Implicitly K should be non-polar, since otherwise the Green function of ℂ \ K with pole at infinity is not the object being discussed.
The variable z ranges over ℂ, and δ is the Euclidean distance dist(z,K).
The phrase 'for sufficiently small δ' should be made explicit as: there exists δ0 > 0, independent of z, such that the inequalities hold whenever dist(z,K) ≤ δ0.
Nearby context notes that any real-line set satisfying this estimate must be of Cantor type; sets with nonempty interior cannot have the same Hölder exponent uniformly near all points of K.

The paper treats this as the Hölder-specialized case of the more general pointwise modulus-of-continuity Problem 2, so the refined question should remain narrowly about Hölder behavior and not drift into the broader modulus problem.
refined_question: Find a non-polar compact set K ⊂ ℝ, regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, such that its Green function g_{ℂ\K} with pole at infinity satisfies a two-sided Hölder estimate near K: namely, there exist α > 0 and constants C1, C2, δ0 > 0 such that for every z ∈ ℂ with dist(z,K) ≤ δ0, one has C1·dist(z,K)^α ≤ g_{ℂ\K}(z) ≤ C2·dist(z,K)^α.
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 2, Problem 3. The only paper-critical additions needed to make it fully stand-alone are the standing Section 2 regularity assumption on K, the meaning of g_{ℂ\K} as the Green function with pole at infinity, and the explicit threshold δ0 independent of z. I do not broaden it to the general modulus-of-continuity Problems 1–2 or to later questions about Markov factors, because the paper isolates the Hölder case as its own separate Problem 3.
